name: application-signal-strength-bars
title: Signal Strength Bars
description: Ascending-height signal bars with an active count derived from a real strength value and a network-type label (5G/LTE) — distinct from connection-status-pill, which is a binary connected/disconnected pill with no signal-quality gradation.
useWhen: Showing cellular or Wi-Fi signal quality on a graduated scale rather than a binary state.
You want the network type (5G/LTE/3G) labeled alongside the bar indicator.
The active bar count should be derived from a real numeric strength value.
avoidWhen: You only need a binary connected/disconnected indicator — use connection-status-pill instead.
You need a percentage-based meter rather than discrete bars — use a progress bar instead.
The network type is irrelevant to the context — omit the label.
responsiveBehavior: The bars and label are a fixed-size inline group that doesn't reflow; place multiple instances in a flex/grid container to stack them.
accessibility: The bar group carries role='img' with an aria-label stating the exact strength, max bars, and network type, since bar height/count alone isn't announced by screen readers.
Individual bars are aria-hidden since the group-level label already conveys the full state.
Active vs inactive bars are distinguished by both fill color and the group label text, not color alone.

variants.title: Signal strength bars
variants.description: Three signal readings (3/4 bars 5G, full 4/4 bars 5G, and weak 1/4 bar LTE) demonstrating the active-bar gradation, on a light surface.
accessibility: Active bar count is derived from the real strength prop compared against each bar's index, never hand-styled per bar.

variants.title: Signal strength bars (Dark)
variants.description: The same three signal readings, adapted for dark surfaces.
accessibility: Active and inactive bar colors meet WCAG AA contrast on dark backgrounds.
